b2-20-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Learning and the Work
b2-20-01.scenario: Under the willows at midday, the farmer asks you, Veres Péter's friend, whether reading books harms the work in the fields.
b2-20-01.prompt: Tell the farmer that learning does not hurt the work, but helps the family.
cues: Say what learning must not harm
b2-20-01.target: A tanulás nem a munka rovására megy, hanem a családunk javára.
b2-20-01.english: Learning does not come at the expense of the work, but to the benefit of our family.
b2-20-01.canDo: I can express trade-offs and disadvantages using rovására ('at the expense of')

b2-20-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What Decides Our Fate
b2-20-02.scenario: In the field, Veres Péter asks you what your life depends on and what happens without knowledge.
b2-20-02.prompt: Tell Veres Péter what life depends on and what happens without knowledge.
b2-20-02.target: Az élet az időjárás függvényében alakul, de tudás híján mindig mások döntenek rólunk.
b2-20-02.english: Life turns out depending on the weather, but for lack of knowledge others always decide about us.
b2-20-02.canDo: I can express conditional dependence using függvényében ('as a function of / depending on')

b2-20-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Studying at Night
b2-20-03.scenario: A neighbour asks you how Veres Péter, a poor farm worker's son, managed to learn so much.
b2-20-03.prompt: Tell your neighbour what Veres Péter did and what he believed.
cues: Say what he believed knowledge could do
b2-20-03.target: Veres Péter éjszaka is tanult, mert hitt abban, hogy a tudás áttöri a társadalmi korlátokat.
b2-20-03.english: Veres Péter studied at night too, because he believed that knowledge breaks through social barriers.
b2-20-03.canDo: I can describe social mobility hurdles and systemic disadvantages

b2-20-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Views
b2-20-04.scenario: A neighbour asks you what the old farmer and Veres Péter think differently about land and learning.
b2-20-04.prompt: Tell your neighbour how the two men's views differ.
cues: Say what the farmer thinks is important
Say what Veres Péter thinks is important
b2-20-04.target: Míg a gazda szerint a föld a fontos, addig Veres Péter szerint a tudás is fontos.
b2-20-04.english: While the farmer thinks the land is what matters, Veres Péter thinks knowledge matters too.
b2-20-04.canDo: I can compare living standards and educational access across generations using míg... addig correlatives

b2-20-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Knowledge Matters
b2-20-05.scenario: The farmer asks you, Veres Péter's friend, to say in one sentence why peasants need knowledge.
b2-20-05.prompt: Tell the farmer why knowledge matters for the peasants.
b2-20-05.target: A parasztok szempontjából fontos a tudás, mert tudás híján mások döntenek a termény áráról.
b2-20-05.english: From the peasants' point of view knowledge is important, because for lack of knowledge others decide the price of the crop.
b2-20-05.canDo: I can compose a formal sociological analysis utilizing compound relational postpositions

b2-20-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Land or Knowledge
b2-20-consolidation.scenario: At the end of the day, the farmer asks you what Veres Péter hopes for the peasants.
b2-20-consolidation.prompt: Tell the farmer what the farmer trusts and what Veres Péter trusts.
b2-20-consolidation.target: Míg a gazda a földben bízik, addig Veres Péter abban bízik, hogy a tudás a parasztok javára van.
b2-20-consolidation.english: While the farmer trusts in the land, Veres Péter trusts that knowledge is to the peasants' benefit.
b2-20-consolidation.canDo: I can confidently formulate tradeoffs and perspective with rovására, javára, and szempontjából
